releases.summary: New setup helper vuln_stack.py (scan, suggest-sources, discover-feeds, find-cpe via services.nvd.nist.gov) and curated catalog.json of verified feeds, GHSA repos and NVD CPEs

New sources ghsa (api.github.com: repository advisories and the advisories of single packages) and nvd (services.nvd.nist.gov: CVEs published for a CPE), with optional GITHUB_TOKEN and NVD_API_KEY, plus --cve-details enrichment from CVE.org (cveawg.mitre.org)

Fixes: snoozed items come back once, a pause also stops the quiet-day CI shortcut, CVE ids are found in the full text of feed entries, check-feeds flags feeds without CVE ids, a partly read source keeps its first cut-off
New command check-feeds tests vendor feeds at setup; a preview digest before the questions; new replies: not affected, snooze, pause until, check CVE, status; version.json has SHA-256 checksums

Fixes: a new or failed source no longer floods the digest with its archive, RSS 1.0 feeds are read, OSV shows every affected package and its own fixed versions, items with the same CVE are linked, KEV ransomware use is shown

The setup interview is step by step: one question about where the stack is described, then short rounds with clickable choices where the assistant has a question tool, and a shortcut to keep the defaults
New step 0: before the questions, the agent reads the stack from the user's own connectors (GitHub, GitLab, wiki), asks only about what it could not find, and can rescan it once a month
First release: sources Cloudflare Radar Zero Wire, CISA KEV, OSV and vendor feeds, EPSS scores, weekly summary, urgent alerts, update check
